intro: If you're living abroad and need a mortgage on a UK property, an expat mortgage broker can help you find lenders who understand overseas income and remote applications. Searching for an expat mortgage broker near me usually means you want someone who can work with you across time zones and currencies. We introduce you to a suitable UK mortgage broker who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for an expat mortgage broker usually need
need_lead: You're likely based outside the UK and need a broker who can handle the extra layers that come with an overseas application.
needs: You want to buy a home in the UK while living and working abroad, and need a broker who understands expat lending criteria.
You need to remortgage a UK property from overseas, perhaps to a better rate or to release equity, and want a broker who can manage the process remotely.
You have income in a foreign currency and need a broker who knows which lenders accept it and how they assess it.
You're planning a move back to the UK and want a mortgage arranged in advance, so you need a broker who can work with your timeline.
You've been turned down by a high street lender because of your overseas address and need a broker who specialises in expat cases.
context_heading: What to understand about expat mortgage advice
context: Mortgage advice is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). Any broker or adviser you use should be authorised, or be an appointed representative of an authorised firm, and you can check this on the FCA register. Advisers typically hold a qualification such as CeMAP.

Brokers must tell you whether they search the whole of the market or a limited panel of lenders, and how they are paid, whether by lender commission, a fee, or both. If something goes wrong, you can complain to the firm and then to the Financial Ombudsman Service.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Tell us where you currently live and where the property is, or will be, located in the UK.
Explain your residency status and how long you've been abroad, as this affects which lenders will consider your application.
Describe your income, including the currency you're paid in and whether it's from employment, self-employment or another source.
Mention the size of deposit you have available and whether it's held in the UK or overseas.
Let us know if you're buying, remortgaging or releasing equity, and whether you have a specific deadline in mind.
Share any previous mortgage applications or credit issues that a broker should be aware of.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the expat mortgage broker
questions: Do you have experience arranging mortgages for clients living in my country of residence?
Which lenders on your panel accept income in my currency?
How will you verify my identity and address remotely?
What is the process for submitting an application from overseas, and what documents will I need to provide?
How do you charge for your services, and are there any fees payable upfront?
What timescales should I expect for an expat mortgage application, and how does that compare with a UK-based application?

faqs.q: Can I get a mortgage in the UK if I live abroad?
faqs.a: Yes, many lenders offer mortgages to expats, but the criteria vary. A broker can help you understand which lenders are likely to accept your situation.

faqs.q: What is a remote ID check and why is it needed?
faqs.a: Remote ID checks allow brokers and lenders to verify your identity without you being physically present in the UK. This is a standard part of the application process for expats.

faqs.q: How does currency affect my mortgage application?
faqs.a: Lenders may assess your income in the currency you earn and convert it to sterling, which can affect how much you can borrow. They may also consider exchange rate fluctuations.

faqs.q: Will I need to pay a fee to the broker?
faqs.a: Brokers must tell you how they are paid, whether by lender commission, a fee, or both. You should ask for this in writing before proceeding.

extra_heading: Making 'near me' work when you live overseas
extra: Searching for an expat mortgage broker near me is a slightly odd thing to do from abroad, because the nearest broker to your overseas address is unlikely to know UK lending rules. What the search usually really means is that you want a UK-based broker you can reach easily by phone, email or video call, and who is used to working with the time difference between your country and the UK.

Distance matters less than availability and familiarity with your situation. When you compare brokers, ask how they handle calls across time zones, whether they have dealt with applicants resident in your country before, and how they keep you updated when documents need to move back and forth remotely. A broker who is quick to respond and clear about the remote process is usually more useful than one who happens to be geographically close to a UK property you own.

It also helps to be realistic about pace. Expat applications often take longer than UK-based ones because identity checks, currency questions and overseas paperwork all add steps, so build in room around any deadline you have. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK mortgage broker free of charge, and they will quote you directly, with fees on application.

extra_faqs.q: Does the broker need to be near my UK property or near where I live abroad?
extra_faqs.a: Neither is essential, because expat applications are handled remotely. What matters is that the broker is authorised in the UK and experienced with applicants living in your country of residence.

extra_faqs.q: Can I speak to a broker at a time that suits my time zone?
extra_faqs.a: Many brokers working with expat clients will arrange calls outside standard UK office hours. Ask about this early so you know how communication will work before you commit.
